item.description:
Scribe opens and saves without freezing, holds downloads to their limits, and never replaces a library that only failed to open.

  • The weekly library backup is made in the background, so a launch when one is due no longer pauses before the window responds.
  • Emptying expired pieces from the bin happens in the background, a few at a time, after the window opens.
  • A backup that fails part-way no longer replaces the last good one.
  • Fixed: if your library couldn't be opened for a passing reason, such as another copy of Scribe holding it, Scribe set it aside and started an empty one. Now it leaves it untouched, says so, and tries again when you ask; anything added meanwhile isn't kept.
  • A damaged library is set aside together with its working files, never over an earlier copy, and put back if starting a fresh one fails.
  • While a library is set aside, Scribe no longer runs its weekly backup or empties the bin, so neither can disturb the preserved copy.
  • A page larger than 30 MB stops downloading as soon as it passes the limit, and says "That page is too large to save" instead of a network error.
  • An article saves at most 300 images, 150 MB in all; any past that keep their web address.
  • A book is held to its size limit by what it actually unpacks, not what its archive claims, and a chapter too large to read is skipped.
  • Saving a page reads and tidies it in the background, so Scribe stays responsive while a long article is saved.
  • Cancelling a save stops it sooner.

Scribe finds pieces saved twice and keeps one copy, and a PDF's find bar and notes stay out of each other's way.

  • New: Settings ▸ Library ▸ Saved twice lists pieces in your library more than once. Keep one copy of each; the others go to the bin, and the one you keep takes their place on the stack, their tags and their category.
  • Fixed: saving a PDF that was already in the library kept a second copy, even with Duplicates set to Skip.
  • Fixed: a book or link saved twice at once, such as two copies in one folder, could get past the duplicate check.
  • Duplicates are recognised more widely: a book with the same ISBN, or the same title with its author written differently, and a link with tracking parameters or "www." added. Two editions of a book with different ISBNs stay apart.
  • Fixed: with a PDF's notes open, the find bar sat off-centre and partly over the notes.
  • Fixed: selecting text near the top of the page while finding could put the highlight picker on top of the find bar.
  • The notes beside a PDF mark the highlight you jumped to, and keep it in view, until you pick another.

Closing Find in a PDF no longer opens the highlight colours.

  • Fixed: clicking Find's close button or arrows in a PDF opened the highlight colours, as if you'd selected the match yourself.
